songs.title: Vātāpi Gaṇapatiṃ Bhaje'haṃ
songs.summary: A prayer to Ganapati enshrined at Vatapi. Dikshitar describes his iconography and his place in the Muladhara chakra, and signs with his mudra 'Guruguha' and the raga's name, Hamsadhwani.

lines.meaning: I worship Ganapati of Vatapi,
the elephant-faced one, the giver of boons.
Whose feet are served by the bhūtas (beings) and others,
who sustains the world made of the elements and all that comes from them,
who is free of attachment and is praised by yogis,
the cause of the universe, the remover of obstacles.
Worshipped long ago by Agastya, the great sage born of a pot,
who dwells at the centre of the triangle (of the sacred yantra),
worshipped by Vishnu (Murari) and the other chief gods,
who resides in the Muladhara, the root chakra,
who is the essence of the four levels of speech, beginning with Para,
the curved-trunked one whose very form is Om,
who always wears the crescent moon on his forehead,
who holds a stalk of sugarcane in his left hand.
Who holds the noose and the citron fruit in his lotus hands,
who is far removed from all impurity, whose form is vast,
whose form delights Shiva (Hara), Guruguha and others,
Heramba (Ganapati), adorned by the raga Hamsadhwani.

songs.title: Nagumomu Ganaleni
songs.summary: Tyagaraja pleads with Rama to come and protect him, unable to bear not seeing his smiling face. He wonders whether Rama's attendants or Garuda are to blame for the delay.

lines.meaning: Knowing my anguish at not seeing your smiling face,

lines.text: nanu brova rādā śrī raghuvara nī
lines.meaning: won't you come and protect me, O Sri Raghuvara?
O bearer of the king of mountains (Govardhana), all those around you —
aren't they the ones who give you good counsel? Would they leave you like this?

lines.text: khagarāju nī yānati vini vega canaledo
lines.meaning: Did Garuda, king of birds, not set off quickly on hearing your command?
Or did he say that the earth is too far from the heavens?
O Supreme Being who rules the world, to whom else can I appeal?
Don't show me indifference, I cannot bear it. Take me as your own, O one praised by Tyagaraja.

songs.title: Bantu Rīti Koluvu
songs.summary: Tyagaraja asks Rama for a soldier's post in his court. His armour, badge and sword are his devotion: the thrill of bhakti, the mark of Rama's devotee, and the name of Rama.

lines.meaning: O Rama, grant me a post in your court, the way a soldier serves.
(The service of one who) starting with Manmatha, the wielder of the sugarcane bow,
strikes down pride and the other inner enemies and fells them to the ground — that true service.
The thrill of devotion that raises the hair, as my mighty armour,
the badge that marks me as Rama's devotee,
and the fine sword that is Rama's name — these
shine on this Tyagaraja, O Lord.
